title: Grateful Dead Live at Winterland Arena on 1967-10-22
lineage: SBD > Rm > Cass > DAT (Sony TCD-D8) > CDR (Tascam CDRW700) > EAC (Plextor 48/24/48 - Secure Mode) > Samplitude v7.0 > SHN

ai_review.summary: A high‑energy 1967 soundboard capture with stellar New Potato, Lovelight and the debut “That’s It” (The Other One) suite.
ai_review.review: This recording delivers a vivid snapshot of the Dead at their psychedelic peak – tight jams, blistering Jerry solos and a powerhouse Pigpen on Lovelight. The show shines on New Potato Caboose, the first full‑blown "That's It" suite and a bluesy Hurts Me Too, while the soundboard source is generally clear despite a few drop‑outs and a cut‑off in Lovelight. Overall it’s an essential early‑Dead document.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 40 reviews, the vast majority rate 4–5 stars and praise both performance and sound; only minor recording glitches are noted, so the combined show‑and‑recording score is very high.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Most reviewers call the audio "great" or "crisp for ’67", though a few note dodgy sections, drop‑outs and the Lovelight cut‑off. Overall the mix is clear enough to hear each instrument.

standout_songs: That's It for the Other One (The Other One suite)
show_quality.setlist_flow: A nonstop, high‑energy psychedelic set that moves from bluesy numbers into extended jams; the only blemish is a mid‑song cut on Lovelight.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His solo is described as blazing, high‑energy and sometimes stumbling but overall a driving force of the show.
band_member_comments.Phil: Praised for tight counterpoint with Jerry on New Potato and solid bass work throughout.
band_member_comments.Bob: Pigpen’s vocals are highlighted as “great” on Lovelight and bluesy Hurts Me Too, with original early lyrics noted.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keyboard/organ described as haunting and funeral‑like at moments; overall strong support for the jams.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill and newcomer Mickey are praised for their seamless interplay and pliability, marking Mickey’s first recorded appearance.
